name: OH-14
label: Likely R

key_factors: Incumbent David Joyce with large cash advantage ($3.1M vs $34K)
No polls or expert ratings; markets price Democrat at ~6%
model.rationale: The district's R+10 lean, Joyce's incumbency and overwhelming financial edge, and prediction markets near 94% Republican all point to a comfortable incumbent win with minimal contrary evidence.
model.watch: Any late polling or outside spending targeting the race would be the first sign of a competitive shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
David Joyce seeks another term in a northeastern Ohio district that leans Republican by about ten points. He enters the general election with a large financial advantage, holding roughly $3.1 million on hand while Democrat Maria Jukic has raised only about $62,000 and has minimal cash remaining. No outside groups are spending against the incumbent.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and prediction markets, which price the Democrat at roughly six percent. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and the money gap points to a comfortable Republican win, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty.
